subject: Q1 invoice — seat count discrepancy
body:
Priya,

We're reviewing the Q1 invoice and the seat count looks off by 31 seats vs what we provisioned end of last year. That's roughly $14k of overage we don't think we owe. Can you pull the audit trail for additions over the past 90 days?

This came up in our finance close yesterday and we need to resolve before next week.

Mike Reyes
CFO, Acme Corp

subject: Re: Q1 invoice — seat count discrepancy
body:
Hi Mike,

Thanks for flagging — let me dig in. Quick context: our seat-count is event-driven, so any user that logged in within the billing window counts as active even if they were deactivated mid-month. That's by design but I know it's not always intuitive, especially against your finance close timeline.

I'll pull the audit trail today and come back to you with a per-seat breakdown by EOD tomorrow. If we find the deltas are dormant accounts that should have been off, we'll true those up.

One ask: would Sarah's team be open to a 15-minute call Thursday to walk through? Sometimes easier than email.

Best,
Priya

subject: Heads up: Acme CFO pushing on Q1 invoice
body:
Hey Lena —

Flagging early. Mike Reyes (Acme CFO) just pushed on a 31-seat overage on the Q1 invoice (~$14k). Renewal is mid-April so the timing is bad.

My read: this is half a real billing-design issue (we count event-active even if deactivated), half a finance-close pressure thing on their side. I think we resolve with a partial credit + a process change for them, but I want to size the credit room before I land on a number.

Nadia — can you pull the seat-event audit for Acme Jan 1 through Mar 1, broken down by user-state at billing snapshot? Looking for how many of those 31 were dormant.

No emergency yet. Will keep you posted.

— P

subject: Re: Heads up: Acme CFO pushing on Q1 invoice
body:
Priya — pulled it. Of the 31 contested seats, 18 were dormant >60 days at billing snapshot, 9 were single-event logins (probably 'check this thing then close'), 4 were genuine active.

If you want to credit, $4.2k is the math on the 18 dormant ($2.4k) + half of the 9 (~$1.8k). I'd not credit the 4 active.

Nadia

title: Acme — Q1 invoice working session
discussion:
Priya walked through the audit trail Nadia pulled. Mike accepted that single-event logins are a gray area and dormant accounts should have been deprovisioned by his team. Some heat about the 'event-active' billing model — Mike says it's surprising and asks if it can be changed in their renewal terms.

Sarah committed to running a quarterly deactivation cleanup going forward. Mike asked for the credit number we'd put on the table.

Renewal timing came up — mid-April. Mike was clear that the credit conversation and the renewal conversation are linked from his side.

title: Acme renewal call — Q1 → Q2 cycle

transcript_segments.speaker: Priya
transcript_segments.text: Hi everyone, thanks for making the time. Quick agenda — I'd like to spend the first ten on outcomes and how the year went, then walk through the renewal proposal and the new billing terms, and then if there's room, touch on the Q3 expansion conversation. Sound good?

transcript_segments.speaker: Priya
transcript_segments.text: Great. So pulling up the value summary — Acme has run roughly 11,200 PO-routing automations and 3,400 supplier onboarding workflows since Jan. That's about 1,900 hours of ops time saved on our model. Sarah, does that match your gut?

transcript_segments.speaker: Sarah
transcript_segments.text: It's a little high but directionally right. The PO routing has genuinely saved my team. Supplier onboarding I'd say half of that — we still do a lot of it manually for the larger suppliers.

transcript_segments.speaker: Priya
transcript_segments.text: Useful, thanks. We can dial that one in. Lena, anything to add on the relationship side?

transcript_segments.speaker: Lena
transcript_segments.text: Just — I want to thank you both. The Q1 billing thing was uncomfortable for everyone and you handled it the best way it could have been handled, which was directly. So thank you.

transcript_segments.speaker: Mike
transcript_segments.text: Appreciate that. Look, we move past it. Let's talk renewal.

transcript_segments.speaker: Priya
transcript_segments.text: Okay. Proposal is 12-month flat at 84k, with the new billing terms — monthly active billed user instead of event-active. 2-year option at 5% off — gets you to 79.8k a year. No surprises in the contract redline.

transcript_segments.speaker: Mike
transcript_segments.text: I prefer the one-year. We're going through some budget realignment in finance and I don't want to lock anything multi-year right now.

transcript_segments.speaker: Priya
transcript_segments.text: Totally fine. One-year at flat. Good.

transcript_segments.speaker: Sarah
transcript_segments.text: Can we talk about the Premium tier? The SSO piece is really what we're after. Our IT just went through a security audit and SSO came up as a finding.

transcript_segments.speaker: Priya
transcript_segments.text: Yes — happy to. Premium adds SSO, advanced audit logs, and a sandbox environment, +18k a year on top of base. SSO is on our Q3 roadmap, currently targeting Sept ship. Hannah from our SE team can do a deep-dive on the tech side if you'd like to bring your IT lead.

transcript_segments.speaker: Sarah
transcript_segments.text: Yeah, let's set that up. I want to bring Raj in.

transcript_segments.speaker: Mike
transcript_segments.text: I'm not committing to Premium today. But if SSO ships in Q3 and the security finding is closed by it, we can revisit at that point. Soft commit, not contractual.

transcript_segments.speaker: Priya
transcript_segments.text: Fair. Let me capture that — soft commit on Premium upgrade in Q3, conditional on SSO shipping and closing your security finding. I'll note it in the renewal recap.

transcript_segments.speaker: Mike
transcript_segments.text: Good. Send me the renewal paper, I'll get it to legal this week.

decisions: New billing terms accepted (monthly active billed user)
Soft commit: Premium tier upgrade in Q3 conditional on (a) SSO shipping, (b) Acme's IT security finding being closed by the upgrade

subject: Some news — and introducing Arjun
body:
Hi Sarah, Mike,

A bit of personal news from my end — I'll be moving on from Northwind in mid-December. It's been a real privilege working with you both since the start of our partnership in early 2023.

Introducing Arjun Mehta, who'll be taking over as your CSM. Arjun has been shadowing me on the account since October and is fully up to speed on your history — the Q1 billing work, the Premium upgrade, the SSO rollout, your QBR cadence. He's also met Raj on the SSO side already.

QBR is on the calendar for Dec 8. Arjun will lead and I'll join as support. Between now and then, please continue routing things to me unless they're forward-looking — Arjun's the right person for those.

Sarah, Mike — thank you both. You've made this account a pleasure.

Best,
Priya
